transcript.text: On the edge of the wool-grey village stood a hollow tree taller than the church, and every winter night a low humming drifted from its bark.
The night her grandmother fell asleep mid-story, Lina put on her red coat and crossed the frosty field to listen.
Inside, a curl of stairs went down, and at the top step sat an old grey fox in a patched green vest named Mosk.
Lina set the last apple of the season on the step; Mosk stared a long while, then tied his vest and stepped down without a word.
